Pakistan imposes emergency rule in province governed by Imran Khan’s party
PM’s office says cabinet move follows ‘provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’.
Authorities in Pakistan have announced a state of emergency in the northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
The state of emergency was invoked on Sunday under two articles of the constitution dealing with security. It effectively suspends the provincial government run by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan.
President Asif Ali Zardari said in a social media post he had approved the recommendations made by the cabinet, which had held a meeting under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif earlier in the day.
A statement issued by Sharif’s office said cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.
Shortly after the announcement, PTI lawmaker Junaid Akbar said Sohail Afridi, the chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, was arrested along with the party’s president in the province.
Six-month duration
The provincial governor will take charge with an advisory council, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad, adding that the arrangement will initially be in place for six months.
PTI spokesperson and Khan aide, Zulfikar Bukhari described the government’s move as “more of a coup disguised as emergency” and warned it would cause “further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage”.
The move comes as the PTI has been preparing for a march on the capital, Islamabad, to demand the release of Khan, who has been in jail for more than three years but still commands widespread popularity across the country.
The march was originally scheduled for September 27 but was postponed until October 4 to allow talks between the government and the PTI leadership to take place.
The government, however, said it would not allow the march to enter the capital and has been preparing for weeks to prevent the arrival of PTI demonstrators in Islamabad. It has erected barriers using shipping containers to block main access routes to the capital.

world-baf75648cc.headline: Saudi Arabia reports injuries in new attack at Riyadh airport, day after strike kills 13
world-baf75648cc.fulltext:
[Text below is CNA's report of the same story — the original outlet blocks automated reading. The link still points to the original.]
One dead in new attack on Saudi airport, a day after Houthi strike kills 13
Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. Eleven people were wounded in addition to the fatality, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.
RIYADH: One person was killed and nearly a dozen hurt in a new attack on Riyadh's international airport on Sunday (Oct 11), Saudi authorities reported, a day after a strike claimed by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.
Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. Eleven people were wounded in addition to the fatality, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.
Coalition forces also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. They later added that a drone had been intercepted and destroyed in the country's Eastern Province, and a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait had been intercepted.
Emergency alerts were also issued in Abha, in the south, early on Monday but the danger had since passed, the Saudi Civil Defense said.
The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the Houthis, who are fighting a ground war in Yemen against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.
Footage released by Saudi state television of the Saturday attack on the Riyadh airport showed scores of religious pilgrims lined up at a gate as they prepared to travel to Islam's two holiest sites. A bright orange flash sent people running in panic, while parts of the roof appeared to cave in.
The airport was closed after the attack, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
HOUTHIS CLAIM RESPONSIBILITY FOR OTHER ATTACKS
In a televised speech on Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack and said the group had struck the airport in Dammam in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and two facilities of Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco.
The Saudi government's media office and Aramco did not respond to requests for comment.
The Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed the strike on Dammam's King Fahd International Airport late on Sunday, adding that "damage assessments and safety inspections of airport facilities are under way."
An eyewitness aboard a taxiing aircraft at Dammam told Reuters that around 8.30pm (1.30am, Monday, Singapore time) on Sunday, they saw a projectile strike the tarmac beside several parked aircraft, causing a fire. The witness said the aircraft returned to the gate. Passengers disembarked and were told to leave.
Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 showed several delays and cancellations on Sunday for arrivals and departures at Dammam airport, the kingdom's third-largest.
The Houthis earlier on Sunday had renewed their warning against using Saudi airports. "We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions," the group said.
Britain's embassy in Saudi Arabia in a post on X advised British citizens against all but essential travel to Jeddah, Dammam and all airports in the kingdom except the airport in Medina.
US aviation authorities issued a notice to US airlines to use caution while flying to or over the kingdom.
"WORSE IS YET TO COME," HOUTHIS WARN
Saudi Arabia has recently stepped up its military involvement in Yemen, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a government counteroffensive after the Houthis seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis said on Sunday that Saudi Arabia carried out 124 air strikes in Yemen in the past 24 hours. "Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said in statements carried by Al Masirah television.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
In a post on Telegram, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said he told his Saudi counterpart that Tehran was ready to help facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen.
ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD
A five-day conference of international energy organisation WPC Energy opened as planned on Sunday at a convention centre about 10km from the Riyadh airport, the Saudi energy ministry said.
A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum also went ahead, according to a media advisory from the ministry. It was not clear which ministers attended.
Italy's energy minister, Gilberto Pichetto Fratin, whose country was co-hosting, had said on Friday he would participate remotely via video link.
German officials were trying to organise a return flight for economy minister Katherina Reiche. She was supposed to return to Berlin from Riyadh on Monday but the ministry said it appeared likely her flight would be unable to take off.
Separately, Saudi authorities announced that in-person classes at schools in Riyadh would be shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday.
Sunday's attack brought the death toll in attacks on Riyadh's airport to 18 for the week. In Saturday's attack, the dead included four Saudis while the remainder were foreign nationals, Saudi authorities said.

global-economics-cf29651af3.headline: Quarter of India’s labour force highly exposed to AI, says report
global-economics-cf29651af3.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
global-economics-cf29651af3.fulltext:
In one of the first such studies of the impact on AI on Indian workforce using India’s own labour data, a new report finds that nearly a quarter of the country’s labour force is engaged in work that is ‘highly exposed’ to AI.
The analysis from the Centre for Finance and Economic Research, Great Lakes Institute of Management took into account data from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).
The higher exposure to AI can have both complementary and substitution effects depending on the job profile with 7.6 per cent of the workforce expected to see increased productivity, while 11.4 per cent may face substitution risk.
However, in a plus, occupations such as agriculture as well as skilled trades — who together account for 54.4 per cent of India’s workforce — face relatively low substitution risk — both from AI or conventional machine driven automation.
The report is authored by Vidya Mahambare, Vivek Jadhav, and Vishnu Venugopalan.
Unveiling the report at an event here on Sunday, V Anantha Nageswaran Chief Economic Advisor, Government of India noted that the task before policymakers is to improve the quality of existing exposure through AI literacy, task redesign, and reskilling.
AI for productivity
Writing in the report’s foreword, the CEA said that employment in high-routine occupations that are susceptible to conventional automation and mechanisation regardless of what happens with AI, has risen by 4.8 percentage points since 2012. AI now competes for routine tasks, he said, stressing that the window to reskill and learn how to use AI for productivity is open.
Health, elderly care, education and the skilled trades, and other non-routine, high-complementarity occupations are areas where India needs more workers, he adds.
Meanwhile, the report mentioned that the share of people in occupations with more substitution risk is higher for younger employee cohorts — at 39.4 per cent in the 15–24 age group. In fact the 15-24 cohort have the worst ratio in terms of high-routine jobs to complementary jobs at 7.6 to 1 against roughly 4 to 1 for every older cohort.
As for the specific States, Maharashtra, Haryana, Kerala and Tamil Nadu have the highest shares of workers in AI-complementary occupations to build on.
As policy recommendations, the report suggested expanding AI literacy and reskilling, particularly for young workers.
“Prioritise young, urban labour-market entrants, the unemployed and those in routine clerical, back-office and low-discretion technical roles for training in judgement, verification, and client engagement,” it said. Also target new AI-induced jobs such as data annotators and AI trainers, it noted, among other recommendations.

global-economics-9c149554ef.headline: Supply-chain shifts, policy push fuel India’s manufacturing startup boom
global-economics-9c149554ef.fulltext:
Nabodita GangulyPublished12 Oct 2026, 06:00 AM IST
New Delhi: Driven by Covid-related supply-chain disruptions and rising protectionism among major economies, India's push to strengthen domestic manufacturing appears to be paying off.
India's manufacturing startups have seen a surge in investor interest and a sharp rise in revenue as the country steps up efforts to boost domestic manufacturing, with funding jumping from $164 million in 2020 when the pandemic arrived to $1.92 billion so far in 2026, according to data platform Venture Intelligence. At the same time, startups such as Pulse, a medical equipment maker, and Scimplify, a specialty chemicals manufacturer and end-to-end supply chain platform, are seeing rising demand from the domestic market.
The total number of deals has also increased from 31 in 2020 to 127 in 2026, according to Venture Intelligence.
“Covid made people realise that having a hedge on the supply side makes a lot of sense. This, in turn, created demand for alternative global supply chains, with India gradually emerging as a reasonably good Plan B. As the domestic market and demand expanded, people also began realising that companies could achieve significant scale before looking to expand globally,” said Abhishek Srivastava, managing partner at early-stage venture capital (VC) firm Kae Capital.
Kae Capital has made several bets on manufacturing, including one of its earliest investments in Zetwerk, a business-to-business (B2B) manufacturing platform that is preparing to go public.
From a macro perspective, escalating trade tensions and tariffs have reinforced the need to diversify supply chains and strengthen domestic manufacturing. While the US-China trade war began in 2018 with tariffs targeting Chinese imports, the Trump administration's 2025 reciprocal tariff policy expanded the use of tariffs to other trading partners, including India, prompting businesses to reassess global sourcing strategies.
Investors once shied away from asset-heavy businesses because their high failure rates left little salvage value if the ventures failed.
“Little value was attributed to intellectual property (IP). The value was attributed only to capital. The beauty today, at least in what we are looking at, is that it is IP-led manufacturing. india-deep-tech-ddb4e8b5bc.headline: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 5- Oct 10]
india-deep-tech-ddb4e8b5bc.fulltext:
This week, 28 Indian startups raised $113.35 million across 3 growth-stage deals, 22 early-stage deals, and 3 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 8 key appointments, 3 fund launches and 2 mergers & acquisitions.
In contrast, 24 startups had collectively secured about $411.46 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $55.3 million across three deals this week, led by lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects, which secured Rs 332 crore (nearly $35 million) in a Series C round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
Smart kitchen appliance startup Beyond Appliances raised Rs 110 crore ($11.4 million) in a Series B round led by Fireside Ventures, while MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth secured Rs 85 crore in equity and debt funding from FMO and LeapFrog Investments.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $58.05 million across 22 deals this week, led by photonic quantum technology startup Quanfluence, which secured $10 million from Chiratae Ventures and Rainmatter, followed by edtech startup byteXL with $9 million from Elevar Equity.
Medtech startup Sunfox Technologies raised $7 million in a Series A round co-led by Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital, while quantum computing startup QpiAI secured Rs 50 crore in debt funding from InnoVen Capital.
Other funded startups included Omnichannel menswear brand Kisah, Wealth management startup Zomint, AI startup Desible.ai, healthtech SuperMush, Cold-pressed oil brand Gramiyaa, among others.
Travel tech platform TravClan, financial information platform MoneyTruVa, and Biofortified staples brand Better Nutrition also raised funding this week but did not disclose the amounts.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru again led the funding charts with 10 startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR and Mumbai with 6 deals and 3 deals respectively. Hyderabad, Dehradun, Chandigarh and others also recorded deals.
E-commerce startups led the sectors with 8 deals, followed by AI and healthtech startups which grabbed 5 deals and 4 deals respectively. Meanwhile fintech, foodtech, SaaS, edtech, deeptech and others also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with 13 deals, followed by pre-seed and Series A startups which grabbed 5 deals each. Series C, Series B, debt and pre-Series A recorded a deal each.
[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding dropped over 72% to $113.35 million from $411.46 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $231.6 million across 22 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Eight key appointments were announced this week. Sorry Sugar named Palash Arneja as Founder and CEO, while Google Cloud appointed Amit Kumar as interim India head. Snabbit appointed Ramesh Srinivasan as Head of Growth and Revenue, ALTEN India named Prabhakar Atla as CEO, and Eggoz onboarded actor Boman Irani as its brand ambassador.
Meanwhile, Genefied promoted Krishna Khandelwal to Chief Sales Officer, Sarvam AI appointed former Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and Chief Business Officer, and OTPless named Geetanshu Singla as CTO.
[Mergers and Acquisitions]
FMCG major Marico acquired an additional 24.09% stake in Plix parent Satiya Nutraceuticals for Rs 1,012.03 crore, while paediatric healthcare company Hoola Health acquired early-childhood development platform UpTodd.
[Fund Launches]
Entrepreneur Navya Naveli Nanda launched Naveli Ventures, the venture arm of the Nanda Family Office, to invest in deeptech, AI, clean energy, space and healthcare startups. Meanwhile, NABVENTURES secured Rs 450 crore in the first close of its second fund, while Recur Club announced a Rs 500 crore fund to provide growth capital to 150-170 D2C brands in FY27.
[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ PhonePe partners with DPCGC to strengthen regulatory compliance in OTT ecosystem
PhonePe has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Digital Publisher Content Grievances Council (DPCGC), a self-regulatory body under IAMAI, to strengthen regulatory compliance in the OTT ecosystem. The partnership aims to simplify self-regulatory organisation (SRO) certification for OTT platforms and online content publishers that use PhonePe’s payment gateway. It will also focus on merchant education and awareness of regulatory requirements under the IT Rules, 2021, which mandate SRO membership for grievance redressal.
▪️ Flipkart expands warehouse capacity by 14 Mn cubic feet ahead of festive season
Flipkart has expanded its supply chain ahead of the festive season, adding 14 million cubic feet of warehousing capacity and extending its delivery network to over 750 new PIN codes. The expansion increased storage capacity by 50%, while automation and technology upgrades boosted peak processing volumes by more than 30% ahead of its Big Billion Days sale.
▪️Pluckk takes its clean-label vision global with UK expansion
Digital-first FMCG brand Pluckk has entered the UK market, with its products available in 17 stores and a 15% share of the protein bar category at these outlets within the first month. The company aims to expand to 100 stores within three months and 500 within a year. It also plans to increase its UK portfolio to over 50 SKUs across clean-label categories, including juices, functional drinks, snacks and salads.
▪️ Pine Labs launches unified payments and customer engagement platform in Singapore
Pine Labs has launched a unified merchant platform in Singapore that combines payment acceptance, acquiring, installment payments and customer engagement services. The platform supports card and alternative payment methods, bank-backed installment plans and rewards through its Fave app. It aims to simplify merchant operations, improve checkout conversions and boost customer retention.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Startup Policy Forum’s DeepVerse platform brings together 30 investors and founders to shape deeptech policy
Startup Policy Forum (SPF) has launched DeepVerse, a deeptech policy platform with 30 partners, including Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed. The initiative aims to address policy challenges across 10 sectors, including semiconductors, spacetech, defence technology, biotech, cleantech and robotics.
▪️ Flipkart’s Big Billion Days returns for 13th edition on October 9 with record seller participation
Flipkart has announced the 13th edition of its flagship festive sale, The Big Billion Days, starting October 9, with early access for select members on October 8. The sale will feature record seller participation, AI-powered shopping experiences and an expanded supply chain network of over 8,200 fulfilment and delivery facilities across India, including Ekart and Flipkart Minutes.
▪️Bengaluru to host Climate Data Week 2026 with over 30 events
The Climate Collective Foundation will host the first edition of Bangalore Climate Data Week from October 12 to 16, with over 30 events across Bengaluru. Supported by Google and Karnataka’s innovation bodies, the initiative is expected to attract over 2,000 participants, including climate tech founders, investors, researchers and policymakers, to explore the use of data and AI in addressing climate challenges.

Eternal’s quick commerce arm Blinkit led India’s major quick-commerce platforms in product availability with an average in-stock rate of 94.4%, followed by Flipkart Minutes at 88.7%, Swiggy Instamart at 83.8% and Zepto at 82.5%, according to a report by brokerage firm Bernstein.

Groww maintained its lead in India’s stock broking market in September 2026, adding over 1 lakh active clients, while Sahi recorded the fastest growth among the top 20 brokers at 11% month-on-month. According to NSE data, the industry’s active client base grew 0.35% to 4.61 crore from 4.60 crore in August, with nearly 1.6 lakh net additions.

BofA expects PB Fintech and Paytm to report strong Q2 FY27 growth but flagged regulatory risks for PB Fintech following IRDAI’s proposed changes to insurance commissions. The brokerage cut PB Fintech’s price target by 19% to Rs 1,145, citing a potential 39-41% decline in EPS in FY28 and FY29, while maintaining a Neutral rating. It retained its Buy rating on Paytm with a target price of Rs 1,775.

deep-tech-7e93f4e163.headline: Tessolve Semiconductor Raises $75 Million from Vector Line Capital
deep-tech-7e93f4e163.fulltext:
Tessolve Semiconductor Raises $75 Million from Vector Line Capital
The US-based semiconductor-focused investment firm marks its first India investment, joining existing backers TPG and Novo Tellus in the Bengaluru company.
Tessolve Semiconductor, a Hero Electronix company, has secured a $75 million investment from Vector Line Capital, a US-based firm that invests exclusively in semiconductors and the semiconductor supply chain. The deal, announced on October 11, 2026, represents Vector Line's first investment in India and adds a third institutional backer to a company that has been expanding its role in global chip development.
The funds are earmarked for acquisitions that extend Tessolve's technical capabilities, service offerings, and geographic presence. The company said it is already in advanced discussions to close multiple acquisitions over the next two quarters, indicating the capital will be deployed relatively quickly.
Vector Line Capital manages more than $1.6 billion and was founded by Geoffrey Baldwin, who spent over three decades in technology investment banking. Baldwin co-founded GCA Advisors, which was subsequently acquired by Houlihan Lokey, where he served as Co-Chairman of the Global Technology Group. Before that, he was a senior member of Morgan Stanley's technology M&A practice. The firm describes its investment approach as supporting companies at critical expansion phases where stable capital and operational alignment can create durable value within the semiconductor ecosystem.
Founded in 2004, Tessolve employs more than 3,500 engineers across 10 countries and operates nine laboratories globally. The company offers end-to-end semiconductor engineering services, covering chip architecture and design through validation, testing, and embedded systems — a breadth of capability that few firms in the sector can match at scale. It counts 18 of the world's 20 largest semiconductor companies among its customers, alongside major hyperscalers and chip startups across end markets that include AI, high-performance computing, automotive, data centers, and industrial applications.
The company's primary technical focus areas are AI, high-performance computing, and analog and mixed-signal chip development. To shorten development cycles, Tessolve uses pre-engineered semiconductor platforms and proprietary design flows, supported by a global lab infrastructure and partnerships with leading foundries, IP providers, EDA vendors, and test equipment companies. It has also been an active participant in India's emerging semiconductor ecosystem, working with new foundries, OSATs, and chip startups developing in the country.
The broader context for the deal is the growing complexity of semiconductor development. As chips become more sophisticated, technology companies have increasingly sought engineering partners capable of carrying work across the full development cycle rather than individual segments of it. Tessolve has positioned itself as one of a small number of firms that can do this across the semiconductor value chain on a global scale.
Tessolve's parent, Hero Electronix, is the technology investment arm of the Hero Group, set up in 2015 to build India-based businesses in sectors including semiconductors, AI, intelligent hardware, design-led manufacturing, and strategic electronics. The platform describes itself as a long-term, evergreen investor that works alongside founders and management teams.
Existing investors in Tessolve include TPG, a global alternative asset manager founded in San Francisco in 1992 with $327 billion in assets under management, and Novo Tellus Capital Partners, a Singapore-based private equity firm with over $1 billion in assets focused on technology and industrial companies across the Indo-Pacific. The addition of Vector Line brings a sector-specific investor with deep relationships across the global semiconductor industry, which Tessolve's leadership indicated was a factor in the investment decision alongside the capital itself.

The company offers end-to-end semiconductor design capabilities, including AI, HPC and analog and mixed-signal chips. It said it works with leading hyperscalers and 18 of the world’s top 20 semiconductor companies.
Tessolve is also in advanced discussions to close multiple acquisitions over the next couple of quarters, it added.

world-991f0ffaa4.headline: Imran Khan’s party decries ‘coup’ after Pakistan suspends provincial government
world-991f0ffaa4.fulltext:
Pakistan has declared a state of emergency in a province led by Imran Khan’s PTI party and suspended its government, a move a party spokesperson described as “more of a coup disguised as emergency”.
President Asif Ali Zardari declared the emergency in the north-western Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Sunday, after the federal government said authorities there had failed to tackle Islamist militancy in the province bordering Afghanistan.
The state of emergency and imposition of a new governor in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa sharply escalates a standoff between Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party and the government, and comes a week after PTI supporters gathered in the province intending to march on Islamabad to demand Khan’s release.
Hundreds of activists and three of Khan’s sisters were detained before the planned march, in what the PTI called one of the strongest crackdowns in years.
Khan’s aide and PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari called the government’s move “more of a coup disguised as emergency,” adding that it risked inciting more bloodshed and instability and was intended to stop the protest.
Pakistan’s constitution allows the government to take over from provincial authorities during an emergency, and the law minister, Azam Nazeer Tarar, said a provincial governor would take charge in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has suffered an increasing number of militant attacks in recent months.
Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad that the governor will initially be in place for six months, but could stay for as long as needed. The interior ministry said it would be deploying troops in the province.
The federal government and the military accuse PTI of failing to curb militants. The party rejects the charge and says Islamabad has not provided the funding and equipment it needs.
Restrictions have been placed on the movements of Sohail Afridi, who had previously been in charge of the province, one of his close aides told Reuters.
Maulana Fazlur Rehman, leader of the JUI-F political party and engaged by the government to mediate with PTI, also condemned the move. “Imposition of emergency is an ambush on democracy,” he told a news conference in Islamabad.
In Islamabad, the government has deployed tens of thousands of security forces and lined roads with containers ready to block roads, to bar protesters from reaching parliament.
Candidates backed by Khan’s party won the most seats in the 2024 election but formed a government only in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Supporters of the 74-year-old former cricket star say the military rigged the vote against him, which the military denies.
Cases against Khan range from concerns over state gifts to instigating violence and an accusation of an unlawful marriage. All but one conviction have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.
President Zardari declared the emergency on the advice of the prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, after a cabinet decision, the president’s office said.
Sharif told the cabinet that security forces and citizens had been under attack for two years. “We can’t just act as a silent spectator.”
Islamabad also accuses Afghanistan of harboring militants who launch attacks inside Pakistan, and says PTI has sympathised with the Taliban in Kabul and its domestic affiliates. Both deny the charge.

H-1B visa curbs could benefit India, says Piyush Goyal
                    Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that tighter H-1B visa access could benefit India. Companies are increasingly moving technology operations to the country, tapping local talent through Global Capability Centres (GCCs).
                                    
Highlights
- Piyush Goyal stated H-1B visa curbs could favour India's tech sector.
- Indian cities like Bengaluru are becoming key hubs for technology work.
- TCS expects no material impact from US PERM program suspension.
- US introduced a $100,000 fee for certain H-1B petitions in 2025.
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said that tighter access to H-1B visas could work in India's favour, as companies increasingly move technology operations to the country.
He believes India could gain economically if more skilled professionals remained in the country instead of moving to the United States. Goyal pointed to Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Gurugram, Noida, and Mumbai as key locations receiving a growing share of technology work.
Companies are increasingly recognising the value of establishing GCCs in India, allowing them to serve international clients through teams based in the country, Goyal stated. He made these remarks at the ET Startup Awards 2026 on Friday.
US immigration restrictions and employment-based residency rules are tightening, affecting technology companies including Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro, and HCL Technologies. The US administration recently suspended new and pending applications under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme.
TCS assessed that this move would not materially affect its business, having filed only a single-digit number of PERM applications over the previous two years. TCS reiterated its plan to recruit 15,000 employees in the US over the next five years. Goyal clarified that he had not discussed H-1B visas or green cards with US officials during his seven-and-a-half years in the role. He distinguished immigration policy from the trade-related movement of professionals, noting that countries determine their own immigration rules.
The US has separately introduced a $100,000 fee for certain new H-1B petitions involving workers hired from abroad in 2025. Goyal also mentioned holding 19 individual meetings with large companies during a recent US visit, as businesses continued to explore opportunities in India.
